<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" />{{GHGcorrected}}</noinclude><section begin="par67"/>by this means is merely intended to make the strengthening of the second radical audible.<ref>Of all the explanations of these separating vowels the most satisfactory is that of Rödiger, who, both for the {{GHGterm|perfect}} and {{GHGterm|imperfect}} (Ewald and Stade, for the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} at least), points to the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}. We must, however, regard {{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וֹתָ}} as formed on the analogy not of {{GHGheb|text=גָּלִ֫יתָ}}, but (with P. Haupt) of a form {{GHGheb|text=גָּל֫וֹתָ}} (= ''gālautā'', cf. Arab. ''ġazauta''), while {{GHGheb|text=תְּסֻבֶּינָה}} follows the analogy of {{GHGheb|text=תִּגְלֶינָה}}. [See also Wright, ''Comp. Gr.'', 229 f.]</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|e}}
The {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תַּ֫מְנוּ}} (for {{GHGheb|text=תַּמּ֫וֹנוּ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=17|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=64|verse=7}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּֽמְנוֹ}} with ''Silluq''), owing to omission of the separating vowel, approximates, if the text is right, to the form of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫מְנוּ}} from {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|f}}
'''5.''' Since the preformatives of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, of the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}}, and of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} throughout, before a monosyllabic stem form an open syllable, they take a ''long'' vowel before the tone (according to {{GHGpar|27|e}}), e.g. {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=יָסֵב}} for ''yă-sēb'', {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=הָסֵב}} for ''hă-sēb'', &c. Where the preformatives in the strong verb have ''ĭ'', either the original ''ă'' (from which the ''ĭ'' was attenuated) is retained and lengthened, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָסֹב}} in {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} for ''yă-sōb'', or the ''ĭ'' itself is lengthened to ''ē'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֵסֵב}} {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} for ''hĭ-sēb'' (see further under h). The vowel thus lengthened can be maintained, however, only before the tone (except the ''û'' of the {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, {{GHGheb|text=הוּסַב}} for ''hŭ-săb''); when the tone is thrown forward it becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, according to {{GHGpar|27|k}} (under {{GHGheb|text=א}} and {{GHGheb|text=ה}} {{GHGterm|compound Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תָּסֹב}}, but {{GHGheb|text=תְּסֻבֶּ֫ינָה}}; {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּסֵב}}, but {{GHGheb|text=תְּסִבֶּ֫ינָה}}; {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=הֲסִבֹּתִי}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|g}}
Besides the ordinary form of the imperfects, there is another (common in ''Aramaic''), in which the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} is pronounced {{GHGheb|text=יִסֹּב}} or {{GHGheb|text=יִסַּב}}, the ''first'' radical, not the second, being strengthened by {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=יִשֹּׁם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקֹּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=26}}; with ''a'' in the second syllable, {{GHGheb|text=יִגָּ֑ר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=11|verse=7}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִדַּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=4}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּשַּׁח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=9}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=יִדֹּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=13}} and frequently, {{GHGheb|text=וָאֶֽכֹּת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=21}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=יִסֹּב}} (''turn'' intrans.) {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=8}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקֹּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=11}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִתֹּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=47|verse=12}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=יִחַם}} (with ''Dageš forte implicitum'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=1}}; in the plural, {{GHGheb|text=יִתַּ֫מּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=35}}, &c. (in pause {{GHGheb|text=יִתָּ֫מּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=28}}); perhaps also {{GHGheb|text=יִמַּל}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִמַּךְ}} (unless these forms are rather to be referred to {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, like {{GHGheb|text=יִדָּ֑מּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִמָּֽלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=24}}); with suffix {{GHGheb|text=תִּקֳּבֶ֫נּוּ}} occurs (cf. {{GHGpar|10|h}}) in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=25}}; {{GHGterm|Imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=יַתֵּם}}, {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=יֻבַּת}}, &c. The vowel of the preformative (which before {{GHGterm|Dageš}} is, of course, short) follows the analogy of the ordinary strong form (cf. also u and y). The same method is then extended to forms with afformatives or suffixes, so that even before these additions the second radical is not strengthened, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּקְּד֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=28}}, &c., for {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּקֹ֫דּוּ|translate=and they bowed the head}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּכְּתוּ|translate=and they beat down}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=44}} (from {{GHGheb|text=כָּתַת}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּתְּמוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִדְּמוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=21}} (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּסֵּ֫בּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֻכַּ֫תּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=20}}). To the same class of apparently strong formations belongs {{GHGheb|text=תִּצַּ֫לְנָה}} (without the separating vowel, for {{GHGheb|text=תְּצִ֫לָּינָה}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=11}} and below, p) ''they shall tingle'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=21|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=19|verse=3}}.—On the various forms of the {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, see under t.
